items.item: [^alignment]: 'In use, the laws let one find ..., an AI reading worked on a language-model judge'; drafts README: 'the laws are used in an audit of a language-model judge'

left.why: Medium, and the old frame: the sentence measures the work by known results right after the purpose sentence, and it is less exact than its note, which gives the proxy problem's scope and Zhuang and Hadfield-Menell's theorems. It is an AI sentence of 3 November in Ren's first person, and restoring version 12 would bring back 'It shows why alignment is hard, and how hard', which 08 §8 lists as more than the laws show. So it is Ren's to read, as the agent left it. A third option, besides the held replacement: cut the sentence. That is version 12 without its over-claim and adds no new words in his voice; [^alignment] keeps the restatement with its scope.

for_ren: Everything the opening agent listed for you still stands: the four restorations of version 12 in your body ('in the model', C's 'likewise states and does not assert', 'I hold that', the thesis clause), the one-sentence header, and the three held body findings not applied.

The header now also names 'the line below this one' (the key line, revised since version 12) and says that 'the line after that and the line before the notes were added since'. The old ledger said this, and the one-sentence version had dropped it.

[^ethics]: 'whether a universal warrant exists is a question the work does not pursue' now reads 'whether a universal warrant exists stays an open question, and what the work offers does not wait on it'. These are the words of the record universal-practical-warrant and of 08 as revised here; 07 §8 still says 'does not pursue'.

[^alignment]: the audit is now said as what it is, 'an AI reading of proved laws worked through for a pipeline with a language-model judge; no test designed from the theory on a deployed pipeline has run'. The earlier wording read as an audit of an actual judge.

My recommendation on 'The work's selection laws restate the proxy problem.': cut it from your body and leave the restatement, with its exact scope, in [^alignment]. The held finding's replacement would put new AI words in your voice, and restoring version 12 would bring back 'why alignment is hard', which 08 §8 says the laws do not show.

Whether the header of your first-person text should say that its revisions are AI-written (AGENTS.md) or leave that to the comment and the history (your 8 November words) is your choice. It is left as the agent wrote it.
